root_cause: Only the Pydantic-model header path is affected. Scalar Header() params already get a hyphenated alias in analyze_param, so they reject underscore headers. For `data: Model = Header()`, request_params_to_args looks each model field up under the hyphenated alias ('x-user-id') but only adds that alias to processed_keys. The next loop copies every unprocessed received key into params_to_process as an 'extra', so an 'x_user_id' header is copied under the field's own name. That means an underscore-only header validates (200 instead of 422), and when both headers are sent the underscore value overwrites the hyphenated one.
best_solution: In request_params_to_args, after `processed_keys.add(alias or get_validation_alias(field))`, also call `processed_keys.add(get_validation_alias(field))`. The field's unconverted name (e.g. 'x_user_id') then counts as consumed and is never copied back in as an extra key. Hyphenated headers still map to the field, underscore-only headers fail with loc ['header','x_user_id'], and extra='allow' models still receive unrelated extra headers. To get there from the statement alone: check that a scalar Header already rejects 'x_user_id' (it does), then try a header declared as a Pydantic model, which is the path that accepts it, and follow the extras loop.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_query_cookie_header_model_extra_params.py adds the model AuthHeaders(x_user_id: str) and the route GET /header-requires-hyphen taking `data: AuthHeaders = Header()`. test_header_model_prefers_hyphenated_header_with_convert_underscores sends both 'x-user-id: hyphenated-value' and 'x_user_id: underscore-value' and expects 200 with {'x_user_id': 'hyphenated-value'}. test_header_model_rejects_underscore_header_with_convert_underscores sends only 'x_user_id' and expects 422 with detail[0].loc == ['header', 'x_user_id']. The existing extra-params tests (extra='allow' models passing extra headers) must still pass.
locating_signals: The statement names `convert_underscores` and 'underscore headers' but not the function, and it does not say the bug is limited to Pydantic-model headers. Grepping convert_underscores in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py finds two places: analyze_param, which is already correct, and request_params_to_args with its processed_keys/extras loop, which is the gold location. The hidden test file name (..._header_model_extra_params) is what shows it is the model path.
our_outcome_summary: v4 PASS (101s, 47 calls): added `processed_keys.add(field.name)` inside the `alias == field.name` branch, which in practice matches gold. v7 PASS (165s, 66 calls): in the extras loop, skipped every header key containing '_'. That passes the tests but goes too far, because it also drops unrelated underscore extras for extra='allow' models. v6 FAIL (130s, 39 calls, 5.5k chars): no source change at all, only repro scripts and test files. Its repro used scalar `x_header: str = Header()`, which already returns 422 at base, so the agent decided the behavior was already correct and never tried a header declared as a Pydantic model. Both hidden tests failed (underscore value won, and 200 instead of 422). v8 FAIL (46s, 33 calls): empty patch.
generalizable_lesson: If a behavior-change statement ('do not accept X') reproduces as already fixed on the simplest API form, do not stop. Grep every code path that reads the option (here there were two sites for convert_underscores) and reproduce through each input shape: scalar param, model/struct param, and extra/passthrough keys. 'Already works' on one path usually means the bug is on another. Also, in code that collects 'unconsumed' keys (extras, kwargs passthrough), mark every name variant you matched as consumed, both the original and the converted one, or the raw variant sneaks back in as an extra.
acceptable_alternatives: Adding field.name, the unconverted validation alias, to processed_keys when convert_underscores rewrote the alias (v4) is equivalent. Skipping every '_'-containing header in the extras loop (v7) passes the hidden tests but also drops legitimate underscore extras for extra='allow' models, so it is fragile under stricter tests.
